root_cause.text: In `drm/arm/display/komeda/komeda_framebuffer.c`, the AFBC framebuffer size validation computed `min_size` as `kfb->afbc_size + fb->offsets[0]` without any overflow check, so a wrapped addition could make an undersized `drm_gem_object` pass the size check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `min_size = kfb->afbc_size + fb->offsets[0];` to `if (check_add_overflow(kfb->afbc_size, fb->offsets[0], &min_size)) goto check_failed;`, and the commit message states the unchecked addition “may incorrectly succeed and allow userspace to provide an undersized drm_gem_object, potentially leading to out-of-bounds memory access.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the kernel overflow helper header so the code can perform safe overflow-checked arithmetic.
intent_record.what: The file adds a new include directive for <linux/overflow.h> near the top of the source, before the existing DRM header includes.
intent_record.how: This makes the overflow-checking helpers and related macros from the Linux kernel available to the translation unit, allowing the code to perform safe arithmetic overflow detection or calculations that depend on those helpers during compilation and runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use overflow-safe addition when computing AFBC framebuffer minimum size to prevent wraparound and enforce correct size validation.
intent_record.what: The code that previously assigned `min_size` by directly adding `kfb->afbc_size` and `fb->offsets[0]` was replaced with a call to `check_add_overflow()`. If the addition overflows, execution now jumps to `check_failed` before continuing.
intent_record.how: This prevents unsigned integer overflow when computing the minimum required buffer size for AFBC framebuffer validation. At runtime, invalid or maliciously large values can no longer wrap around and bypass the size check, which makes the bounds validation reliable.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is an integer overflow in framebuffer size validation. Adding the kernel overflow helper header is directly related because it enables overflow-checked arithmetic needed to fix that bug.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the AFBC framebuffer minimum size calculation by using overflow-safe addition, preventing the wraparound that allowed undersized GEM objects to pass validation.

candidates.rationale: This is the exact pre-fix AFBC minimum-size computation that can overflow when adding fb->offsets[0] to kfb->afbc_size, allowing an undersized drm_gem_object to incorrectly pass the size check.

vuln_statements.explanation: This AFBC framebuffer minimum-size calculation adds fb->offsets[0] to kfb->afbc_size without overflow checking. A wrapped sum can produce a too-small min_size, causing undersized drm_gem_object instances to pass validation.
